title: 21-day Flex Probe: Infra Contract-Onboard Playbook
collaborators: Marco Liu; Priya Nair; Samir Khan
tags: onboarding; hiring; rubric; contract-to-perm; infra; sre; interview; checklist; experiment
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a rapid, evidence-first path for hiring and onboarding short-term infrastructure/serving-runtime engineers (8-24 week engagements) where teams want a low-friction way to validate fit. Goals: 1) validate technical and collaboration fit via a paid 21-day probe, 2) produce concrete artifacts that accelerate a potential perm conversion, and 3) yield structured feedback aligned to onboarding milestones so managers can make forward-looking hiring decisions.

Audience and scope:
- Owners: People Ops + Hiring Manager (Infra / Serving Runtime).
- Panel: interviewers, SRE buddy, platform contacts.
- Candidate types: contractors, contractor-to-perm, emergency flex-hires.
- Excludes executive searches and long-term IC ladders.

Success metrics (pilot targets):
- Probe-to-perm conversion >= 35% within 12 weeks.
- Median days to first merged PR post-conversion <= 30.
- 3-month retention post-conversion >= 85%.
- Panel inter-rater correlation >= 0.6.

Candidate lifecycle (condensed timeline):
- Days 0-7: screening + asynchronous take-home (8-12h).
- Days 8-14: live design/coding interview with rubric scoring.
- Day 15: contract offer for 21-day paid probe (start date agreed).
- Probe Days 1-21: hands-on mini-project inside a sandbox repo with planned deliverables.
- Days 22-25: evaluation meeting and decision (convert / extend / end).

Interviewer rubric (one-page anchor):
Scoring model: 1-4 per dimension (1=insufficient, 2=needs coaching, 3=independent, 4=mentor/stretch). Use weighted total to drive decisions.
Weights (sum 100):
- Systems debugging & incident triage: 30
- Serving/runtime architecture & orchestration: 20
- Observability & SLO-driven troubleshooting: 15
- Code quality & automated tests: 15
- Communication & asynchronous collaboration: 10
- Security & basic compliance hygiene: 10

Rubric cues (prompts for interviewers):
- Systems debugging: ask about OOMs, GPU vs host memory, reproducing flakies, mitigations. Want concrete repro steps and isolation strategies.
- Serving/runtime arch: look for knowledge of batching, KV cache tradeoffs, model variant fallback patterns, autoscaling tradeoffs. Preference for examples from production.
- Observability: expect proposals for metrics, traces, and sampling strategies; read tail-latency numbers and explain remediation.
- Code & tests: small, testable PRs preferred; candidate should explain test choices and rollout approach (canary, feature flag).
- Communication: clarity in written design notes and PR descriptions; ability to summarize tradeoffs for PMs.

Asynchronous take-home probe (short):
- Timebox: 8-12 hours total (candidate may split time).
- Deliverable: a small PR to sandbox repo with README, short design note (300-600 words), tests, and a demo script or short screencast.
- Example prompts: implement a batch-size histogram metric export; add a conservative KV-cache eviction heuristic; or a lightweight admission controller that gates quantized models by compatibility.
- Evaluation: correctness, tradeoff clarity, test coverage, and reviewer friendliness.

21-day paid probe (on-contract workplan):
Week 1 (days 1-7): orientation, environment setup, two small tickets (focus on measurement & reproducibility). Deliverable: one merged PR + experiment note.
Week 2 (days 8-14): mid-sized ticket touching serving config or observability; paired check-ins. Deliverable: draft PR and short demo.
Week 3 (days 15-21): cross-team stretch task (platform + product touch). Deliverable: runbook draft + rollout plan and final demo to hiring manager.
Evaluation meeting (days 22-25): hiring manager + two reviewers + candidate self-eval. Scores via rubric determine conversion, extension with remediation, or end.

Conversion thresholds (practical guide):
- Convert: average rubric >= 3.0 and at least two dimensions scored 3+ AND Week 3 deliverable shows cross-team clarity.
- Extend: average 2.5-3.0 with explicit remediation plan (30 days).
- End: average < 2.5 or unfixable security/access gaps.

Operational first-week checklist (manager responsibilities):
- Pre-Day-1: create seat, GitHub access, VPN & MFA, Slack invite, daily 30-min standup calendar, sandbox repo fork.
- Day 1 AM: manager intro (30m). SRE buddy pairing (1h). Review probe scope.
- Day 1 PM: run environment setup guide, execute demo script, confirm tests.
- Days 2-5: complete two tickets, mid-week unblock 1:1. End-of-week: demo + experiment note submitted.

Security & compliance guardrails (minimum):
- Use synthetic datasets only; probe repos must not contain customer PII.
- KMS/secret access: least privilege and audited; short-lived creds where possible.
- Any access to prod-like infra requires SRE sign-off and scoped credentials.

Communication templates (copy/paste snippets):
- Contract offer email: "Hi [Name], we'd like to engage you for a paid 21-day probe focused on [area]. Start date: [date]. Compensation: [rate]. Objective: deliver two merged PRs and a runbook trial. Please confirm by [date]."
- Team Slack announcement: "Welcome [Name], joining as flex-hire for 21 days to work on [brief]. Buddy: [name]. Please add relevant context."

Scoring sheet (copy/paste):
Candidate: __________________  Panelist: __________________  Date: ______
1) Systems debugging (1-4): ____  2) Serving/runtime arch (1-4): ____  3) Observability (1-4): ____  4) Code & tests (1-4): ____  5) Communication (1-4): ____  6) Security basics (1-4): ____  Weighted total: ____
Notes:
- Strengths:
- Risks / unknowns:
- Suggested ramp plan if converted:

Remediation path (if marginal but promising):
- 30-day focused plan with measurable deliverables.
- Weekly 1:1 and end-of-week demos.
- Minimum 4 pairing sessions in first 30 days.
- Re-evaluate at day 30 for conversion.

Hiring manager conversion checklist (post-probe):
- At least 2 independent pieces of merged work or clear deploy path.
- Runbook and at least one observed SLO/metric change.
- Peer feedback from >=2 teammates confirming collaboration and ownership.
- People Ops signoff on compensation and headcount.

Risks and mitigations:
- Unpaid labor perception: mitigate with paid short-term engagement, finite scope, and documented outcomes.
- Scoring inconsistency: run calibration sessions and provide score anchors.
- Security exposure: enforce synthetic data, short-lived creds, and SRE oversight.

Appendix: copyable short probe prompt:
"Pick one: A) instrument batch-size histogram & export as Prom metric, B) add conservative evict-on-oom heuristic for KV cache, or C) write admission control for quantized model variants by runtime compatibility. Include README, tests, and short demo. Timebox: 8-12 hours."

Revision notes:
- 2025-11-03 Lena Ortiz: draft playbook.
- 2025-11-07 Marco Liu: added rubric weights and probe examples.
- 2025-11-10 Priya Nair: tightened security checklist and conversion criteria.

Open questions for pilot:
- People Ops: finalize compensation band for 21-day paid probes.
- Which teams opt in for Q1 pilot (suggested: serving-runtime, platform, infra).
- Schedule a 60-minute panel calibration workshop.

Next actions (owner: People Ops):
1) Finalize compensation & legal template by 2025-11-20.
2) Run calibration workshop with hiring managers by 2025-11-28.
3) Pilot up to 4 candidates in December and capture outcome metrics.

End of document.
